continuity_scope: Zero-character audit bound to Guy Gavriel Kay's original English The Lions of Al-Rassan, first published in 1995. The audit does not merge any proposed screen adaptation, commentary, review, later work in the broader setting, translation, or historical source with this novel witness.
coverage_rule: No characters are included until a primary novel witness with stable chapter or page locators is available. One bibliographic/fiction-versus-history boundary term is retained from authorized-site metadata; no internal story terminology is inferred.
omissions: All named characters, relationships, religious and political terminology, events, and plot claims from the novel, pending primary-text locators.
All film, television, game, and other adaptation material.
Author/site commentary and reviews as story-canon evidence.
uncertainties: The accessible authorized Guy Gavriel Kay site identifies the novel and describes its fictional setting as inspired by medieval Spain, but does not supply a primary-text chapter/page witness adequate for canonical character claims.

Jaddites, Asharites, Kindath, Esperaña, and Al-Rassan must remain fictional source-specific constructs; this audit makes no direct equation to Christianity, Islam, Judaism, medieval Iberian peoples, or historical polities.
The available orientation metadata signals conflict among beliefs and a violent history; specific war, persecution, relationship, or outcome claims are deferred pending text access.
evidence_basis: Authorized Bright Weavings work metadata identifies the 1995 novel and its fictional Al-Rassan/Esperaña setting. No accessible primary text with stable chapter/page locators was verified, so it is not used to create character or relationship records; the sole source term is an explicitly bibliographic/fiction-boundary record.

supports: Novel identity, 1995 first-publication metadata, and the setting's fictional historical-fantasy framing.
Original UK HarperCollins hardcover and edition-separation context.
